Creature abilities

Abilities are shown as icons on a creature; hold the pointer over an icon for its name. The table lists the most common ones under their names in the games. Numbers in brackets vary by creature.

AbilityWhat it does
FlyingCan be blocked only by flying creatures.
Cannot attackWalls: they defend but never attack.
First StrikeHits before its opponent, in attack and in defence.
Regeneration (1–3)When destroyed, can come back by paying the given cost.
TrampleDamage left after destroying its blockers goes to the enemy hero.
LifetapDamage to the enemy hero heals its owner.
RestlessDoes not rest after attacking.
DisenchantRemoves the enchantments of creatures it hits.
Creature cannot get upDoes not recover by itself after resting.
BerserkMust attack whenever it can.
Ether DefenseCannot be the target of spells or abilities.
UnblockableCannot be blocked.
HasteCan act on the turn it is summoned.
ElusiveCan be blocked only by walls.
Team attackerAttacks only together with a creature of its race.
PoisonousDestroys a creature it damages in combat.
Discard (1–3)When it damages the enemy hero, the opponent discards that many random spells.
Pale ability, Pale aspectEtherlords II: the creature can pass into its pale aspect, where it neither attacks nor is attacked.
Spell jammingEtherlords II: hinders the opponent's spells.

Many creatures also have abilities you use by resting them or paying ether; their own descriptions explain them in the game. See Attack and defence for how the combat abilities work together.
